This is a controlled, safe operation limited to class-defined attributes - not user-controlled input. The pattern is intentional and secure.

findings.reasoning: This is a false positive. The code implements a standard transparent proxy pattern. The __getattr__ method is explicitly designed to forward attribute access to the wrapped object. This is the intended use case for __getattr__ - it only gets called when an attribute is not found on the proxy object itself. The 'name' parameter is the attribute name being accessed, which is how proxies work. There is no vulnerability here - this is a fundamental Python idiom for creating transparent proxies.

evidence.code_context: StreamWrapper is a stream wrapper class that acts as a transparent proxy. It wraps a stream object (like stdout) and forwards attribute access to the wrapped stream via __getattr__. This is documented in the class docstring and is the standard way to implement proxies in Python.
evidence.dataflow_analysis: The 'name' parameter to __getattr__ is the attribute name being accessed on the wrapper object. When an attribute is not found on StreamWrapper, Python automatically calls __getattr__ with the attribute name. This is then used to look up the same attribute on the wrapped object.
evidence.notes: This is the standard proxy pattern in Python. The __getattr__ special method is specifically designed for transparent attribute forwarding. There are also special cases handled separately (__enter__, __exit__, __setstate__, __getstate__, write, isatty) which are properly delegated or overridden.
